how_md: Each level is a **checklist**. Your tutor marks every item from your lessons (with evidence), and you rate yourself too. **Not checked** = we haven't tested it yet. Grammar and linking items are about **understanding** them when you read or hear them – speaking and writing come later.

sources.name: CEFR Companion Volume (Council of Europe, 2020) – can-do descriptors
British Council / EAQUALS Core Inventory for General English
CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 & Grammar Profile (Tono Laboratory, TUFS) via Open Language Profiles

levels.name: A2 · Elementary
levels.summary_md: You can understand **simple, everyday English** when people speak slowly and clearly.
proof: Understand a slow graded audiobook (level 2) without the text
Read a short simple email or menu without a dictionary

items.text: Understand words and phrases about personal life, shopping, local area and work
Catch the main point of short, clear messages and announcements
Follow a slow, clear everyday conversation about familiar things
Find specific information in simple everyday texts: ads, menus, timetables
Understand short, simple personal messages and emails

sections.name: 🧩 Grammar (understand it when you read/hear it)

items.text: Past simple – regular and irregular
items.ex: She **went** home and **called** her mum.

items.text: Past continuous
items.ex: I **was walking** when it started to rain.

items.text: Present perfect – basic
items.ex: I**'ve been** to London. Have you **finished**?

items.text: Future: will / going to / present continuous for plans
items.ex: I**'m meeting** Tom tomorrow.

items.text: Modals: can, could, should, must, have to, might
items.ex: You **should** take an umbrella.

items.text: Comparatives and superlatives
items.ex: It's **cheaper** than… · the **best** sandwich

items.text: much / many / a few / a little
items.ex: There's **a little** milk, but **not many** eggs.

items.text: First conditional
items.ex: **If** it rains, I**'ll** take the tram.

items.text: Common phrasal verbs
items.ex: get up, look for, find out, turn off

items.text: and, but, or, because, so, then, when
items.ex: I was tired, **so** I went to bed.

items.text: Describe your family, work and daily routine in simple sentences

levels.name: B1 · Intermediate
levels.summary_md: You can understand the **main points** of clear standard English about familiar things – work, free time, everyday life – and follow podcasts made for learners.
proof: 6 Minute English (BBC): understand ~80% on the first listen, without the transcript
Read a graded reader (level 4–5) at a comfortable speed, without translating

items.text: Understand the main points of clear standard speech on familiar topics (work, free time, daily life)
Follow the main points of podcasts/videos on topics you like when speech is fairly slow and clear
items.ex: e.g. 6 Minute English, Easy English

items.text: Follow most of a conversation between two people about everyday things
Hear the small squeezed words in natural speech: I'd, you'll, it's, she's, d'you
items.ex: I'd better go. · You'll get used to it.

items.text: Understand simple directions, instructions and announcements
Understand texts written mostly in everyday or work language
Understand descriptions of events, feelings and wishes in stories and messages
Find and understand what you need in emails, notices and short articles
Read an easy story at normal speed without translating in your head
See the main argument of a clear text (not every detail)
Follow what it / this / that / which refers to
items.ex: …sounds right. **This** is because…

sections.name: 🧩 Grammar (understand it when you read/hear it)

items.text: Present perfect vs past simple (for/since, already, yet, ever)
items.ex: I**'ve lived** here **since** 2020. · I **moved** in 2020.

items.text: Present perfect continuous
items.ex: I**'ve been waiting** for an hour.

items.text: Past perfect
items.ex: When I arrived, the film **had started**.

items.text: Passive – present and past
items.ex: It **was built** in 1900. · English **is spoken** here.

items.text: Second conditional
items.ex: **If** I **had** more time, I **would** read more.

items.text: Reported speech: said that / told me to / asked if
items.ex: She **told me to** wait. He **asked if** I was OK.

items.text: Relative clauses: who, which, that, where
items.ex: the café **where** Jess works

items.text: Verb + -ing or to-infinitive
items.ex: enjoy **doing** · decide **to do** · suggest **doing**

items.text: be / get used to + V-ing  vs  used to + V
items.ex: I'm **used to getting up** early. · I **used to live** there.

items.text: too … to / … enough to
items.ex: It's **too far to** walk.

items.text: Question tags
items.ex: It's cold, **isn't it**?

items.text: although / even though / however / though – contrast
items.ex: **Although** he was tired, he helped.

items.text: unless / as long as / in case – conditions
items.ex: I can't sleep **unless** it's dark.

items.text: so that / in order to – purpose
items.ex: I left early **so that** I wouldn't be late.

items.text: Time & order: while, during, after that, finally, as soon as
Everyday chunks: it takes + time, spend time doing, I'd rather, had better
items.ex: It **takes** 20 minutes. I'd **better** go.

items.text: rather / instead / in other words
items.ex: He didn't text. **Rather**, he called.

items.text: Tell a simple story or describe an experience
Write a simple email or message about your day or opinion

levels.name: B2 · Upper-intermediate
levels.summary_md: You can understand **standard English at natural speed** – podcasts, news, interviews, longer articles with opinions – about most topics, not only familiar ones.
proof: A normal podcast for native speakers (e.g. TED-Ed, a news podcast): ~80% on the first listen
Read a newspaper opinion article and explain the writer's view

items.text: Understand standard speech at normal speed, on familiar and new topics
Follow a longer talk and its line of argument if the topic is fairly familiar
Understand most news, documentaries, interviews and podcasts in standard English
Follow a lively conversation between native speakers (with some effort)
Hear the speaker's attitude: doubt, irony, enthusiasm
Understand articles and reports where the writer has a point of view
Read quite independently, changing speed for different texts; dictionary only sometimes
Read modern fiction and non-fiction at a natural pace
Scan a long text quickly to find the details you need

sections.name: 🧩 Grammar (understand it when you read/hear it)

items.text: Passive in all tenses + have something done
items.ex: It **has been fixed**. · I **had my hair cut**.

items.text: Third and mixed conditionals
items.ex: If I **had left** earlier, I **would have caught** it.

items.text: wish / if only
items.ex: I **wish** I **had** more time.

items.text: Future continuous and future perfect
items.ex: This time tomorrow I**'ll be flying**. By 6, I**'ll have finished**.

items.text: Modals of deduction about the past
items.ex: She **must have** forgotten. He **can't have** seen it.

items.text: Non-defining relative clauses and preposition + which/whom
items.ex: , **which** surprised everyone · the person **to whom** I spoke

items.text: Participle clauses
items.ex: **Having finished** work, he went home.

items.text: Past perfect continuous
items.ex: I **had been waiting** for an hour.

items.text: Reporting verbs with patterns
items.ex: He **denied taking** it. She **warned me not to** go.

items.text: whereas / while / on the other hand / nevertheless – contrast
as a result / therefore / consequently / due to – cause and result
moreover / furthermore / in addition – adding
Hedging: tend to, seem to, it is likely that, arguably
Common idioms and phrasal verbs in everyday speech
items.ex: get the hang of, give it a go, run out of

items.text: Explain your view on a topic, with pros and cons

levels.name: C1 · Advanced
levels.summary_md: You understand **long, complex** speech and texts, even when ideas are only implied – fast conversations, different accents, idioms, style.
proof: A fast, unscripted podcast between native speakers (e.g. Hard Fork): ~85–90% without effort
Read a long feature article or a novel and catch the tone and irony

items.text: Understand long speech even when it isn't clearly organised and links are only implied
Understand a wide range of idioms, slang and changes in tone
Follow fast group conversations with different accents
Watch YouTube/podcasts for native speakers without much effort
Understand long, complex texts and notice differences in style
Understand specialised articles outside your field (re-reading difficult parts)
Catch implied meaning, attitude and irony

sections.name: 🧩 Grammar (understand it when you read/hear it)

items.text: Inversion for emphasis
items.ex: **Hardly had I** arrived when… · **Not only was he**…

items.text: Cleft sentences
items.ex: **What I need is** sleep. · **It was** Tom **who**…

items.text: Advanced passive
items.ex: He **is said to have** left.

items.text: Advanced modals
items.ex: You **needn't have** come. · It **may well** rain.

items.text: Ellipsis and substitution
items.ex: **So do I.** · I hope **so**. · **If not**, …

items.text: Formal linkers: albeit, hence, thereby, notwithstanding
Spoken markers: mind you, that said, having said that, as it were
Speak fluently and naturally about complex topics
